You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testNullRecordSeparatorCsv106` in `CSVFormatTest` is testing the behavior of the `format` method in `CSVFormat` class. The test sets up a CSV format with a semicolon separator, skips the header record, and specifies headers "H1" and "H2". It then formats the values "A" and "B" using this format and checks that the resulting string does not end with "null". However, the test fails because the actual output is "A;Bnull" instead of the expected "A;B".

The incorrect behavior reported by the user is consistent with how the `format` method is handling the record separator. It appears that the record separator is being incorrectly appended to the formatted string even though there are no additional fields after "B".

To further investigate the issue and locate the potential bug, we need to examine the implementation of the `format` method in the `CSVFormat` class.

Next, let's retrieve the code snippet of the `format` method in the `CSVFormat` class to understand how the record separator is handled there.

messages.content:
The `format` method in the `CSVFormat` class takes an array of `Object` values and uses a `CSVPrinter` to print the record. The method then trims the output before returning it as a `String`.

Given that the output in the failing test is "A;Bnull" instead of the expected "A;B", it seems like the record separator is being appended to the formatted string even when there are no additional values after "B". This behavior is likely causing the discrepancy between the expected and actual outputs.

To fix this issue and prevent the unnecessary addition of the record separator, we should modify the logic in the `CSVFormat.format` method to handle cases where the last value is the end of the record without appending the separator.

The potential fix for this issue would involve updating the logic in the `CSVFormat.format` method.

Next, let's suggest which method needs to be fixed to address this bug.
`org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat.format(java.lang.Object...)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
